The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

I try to make it a home away from home for them.  For me it is like having a large, ever changing family.
Because of the changing politics throughout the world, much of which is troubling,  as angry people take over governments and spread upset and anger about, I think it is valuable to have platforms such as Airbnb bringing people together from everywhere.  The chance to meet, talk, share a meal, converse with a group of people from different countries has to be good for our world.  I have a large map of the world in the living room and each guest puts a pin in the country from which they come.  It is thrilling to see the map fill and know that we have had good times with friends from all of those places!

neighborhood_overview:
My home is in a quiet residential neighborhood in the foothills of San Jose. There are fields surrounding the neighborhood, and abundant wildlife - it's like living in the country but only minutes away from everything in the valley. Guests are often enchanted by the variety of wildlife that can be seen from my house, and surprised by how quickly they can get places.

If you’re interested in hiking, trail running or even a little mountain biking, you’ll like Alum Rock Park which is quite close to my house. It’s a beautiful park in the foothills that reminds people of a little Yosemite – there’s even a stream running through it. You can do a web search and get the official park info, and Yelp has great reviews where people have added 470! photos.
host_about:
I love having guests and I'll do everything I can to make sure you have a wonderful stay in my home.  I'm especially proud of my status as a Superhost and I work hard to maintain that (we're re-evaluated every 3 months). Even after 9 years as a host I feel like every guest is a new friend and look forward to meeting them. 

For those guests new to Airbnb, I want to make sure your first experience is a complete success; and for those who’ve stayed in an Airbnb before, I want to make sure your stay with me is the best you've experienced.

A little about me. I'm sort of retired, after 20+ years as a software engineer, and a couple of other careers as well. 

Things I like to do:  travel, hike, cook, garden, bicycle, train dogs, go to art galleries, of which we have many in the Bay Area, opera, ballet and the theater, and spend time with friends and family.  I especially like DIY projects on my own home. 

I've been interested in California native plants for a while and I'm beginning to add them to my yard. Recently I've become a Master Gardener so these days I spend a lot of time outside, often in Alum Rock Park and on plants and gardening. 

Another of my passions is working with rescued dogs, especially German Shepherd Dogs. I also volunteer with our Wildlife Center of Silicon Valley taking care of injured and orphaned wildlife and releasing them back into the wild.

My experience with Airbnb has been fantastic! Meeting lots of new people from many different cultures, I'm learning about those cultures and countries, and finding out about ethnic restaurants nearby that I've never tried. All my 300+ guests, from 25 countries, have been wonderful.  I've been very lucky and thank Airbnb for their part in making my experience such a good one. 

Several of my guests have found permanent homes here in Silicon Valley and I love to get together with them.

I’m looking forward to meeting you.

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

Pacific Heights is one of the nicest historic neighborhoods that is centrally located in San Francisco.
Walking distance to five grocery stores - three blocks to either Whole Foods (one the corner or California street and Franklin street) or Molly Stones (on California street, after you pass Fillmore street). Also fun grocery Japanese supermarket - 3 blocks and another ethnic one - Woori, Korean market.

It’s a great place to hike and run. I usually run to the Bay and sometimes to the Golden Gate Bridge and back through Lyon Stairs. Very scenic route. There are lost of beautiful parks close to my home. The closest park is just a 1.5 blocks away - on Laguna and Sacramento street.

My home is located close to the famous Fillmore Street and an easy walk to Union Street. Both streets are a shopping heaven. Also there are many great restaurants walking distan
host_about:
I am a physician and I moved to USA 22 years ago. I love what San Francisco city and the Bay Area has to offer. I feel very lucky and privileged to live in a beautiful and safe area of San Francisco called Pacific Heights. 

I am an avid mountaineer/climber and I travel usually once a year, for a month - long expedition trip. That is usually when I open the calendar in AirBnB for my apartment, as well as (separately) for my garage. 

I would like to rent my beautiful home to someone reliable for all that time when I am gone. 

The things I can't live without are my family, friends, mountains, my amazing home, nature, meditation and any kind of physical activity daily. 

My favorite travel destinations - to many to mention. I feel amazing in high altitude mountains. 

I climbed all the highest mountains in the world called Seven Summits (including Mt.Everest), as well as skied to the South Pole.  Beside that, all my travels and expeditions left me with amazing memories. 

My favorite books - too many to list here as I  read a lot, but I love the most  "Master and Margarita" by Michail Bulhakov. There are many books in my home, so if you have time feel free to read something new. I switched now to ebooks or audiobooks, as it doesn't take any physical space. 

My favorite food is prepared with local and organic ingredients - check out many restaurants on Fillmore street - you will have so many to choose from, even after Pandemic years. I love sushi and the best sushi in the city is a walking distance from my home - check out Tataki restaurant (on California street/Divisadero street) - amazing and fresh! 
I also would encourage you to check “State Bird Provisions”, but you would need a reservation. It’s a 7 -10 minutes walking distance from my home. Located on Fillmore street. 

I travel a lot for business - Marriott hotels, but for fun - I prefer staying in a tent or in a cool Airbnb place in different cities all over the world. 

My motto in life is to live largely, “on the edge of my comfort zone", hence climbing or polar expeditions, and now posting my home at Airbnb website. 

Throughout the process of renting my home I learn that my HOA’s CC&Rs (Homeowners Rules) do not allow for any short term rentals and I can only rent it for a month or longer. 

My modern apartment is located on the top floor of the beautiful Victorian (freshly painted) building (originally from 1896). I have the best view of Japan Town and Twin Towers as well as complete privacy in my home. 

I love green plants and I have many in my home and at the balcony. I’ll be very grateful if you could please water it once a week ( just a little bit :) to keep it lush and green. 

So far, I had wonderful guests from all over the world for the last ten years. I am super grateful for all people I met through AirBnB. 

Please feel free to ask me any questions before you send a reservation. 

I look forward to meeting you in person and to host you in my home.
 
Thank you.

name: Condo in San Francisco · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 bath
host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

We have lived in the San Francisco area for almost 50 years and purchased our San Francisco home in 1999. In 2004 we began to spend time away and a friend suggested we offer it to guests on vacation or in San Francisco on business. We soon learned that people really enjoyed our home-like atmosphere. We are thrilled with the response we have gotten and we work hard to keep our new and returning guests contented and feeling cared for. Visitors say they appreciate our clean and well appointed home and our knowledge of the city and professional attitude.

Most guests mention the feeling of a being in a real home as soon as they enter. We think this is because we still live there part of each year and keep the house comfortable and well maintained not only for our guests but for ourselves as well. We are also proud of our garden, keeping it maintained even while we are away. We paint, scrape, clean, renew, update and replace parts of the house every time we come to visit. We think it shows. 

Our guests certainly enjoy our home. Read the reviews! 170 Five Star ratings on HA/VR and 75 on TA. We get these ratings not because everything is always perfect (we do try, however!) but because we go out of our way to help our guests settle in and feel at home and we respond quickly to any question. Finally, if you are bringing a car, you will absolutely love our little garage (for economy to mid-size cars). Parking rules in SF can make you dizzy. If you don't bring a car - great! - hop on the bus one block from the front door and head downtown or to the beach.

You can read more about our home at YourHomeInSanFrancisco. 
Thanks!

host_about:
Welcome to HacknSleep! Hacknsleep provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

We partner with startup accelerators, bootcamps, coding academies, and co-working spaces and prefer recruiting our residents through peer-recommendations and our networks. So please let us know how you have heard from us.

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

host_about:
I moved to California from Bettendorf Iowa in 1979 at 17 years old with a suit case and $300.00 in my pocket to go to college.  I received  a BFA / a Bachelor's Degree in the Fine Arts, with a concentration in drawing an painting in 1984.  I began working in glass my final semister at San Jose State University and immediately began designing and fabricating large scale murals that are sandblasted in glass for various glass studios in the San Francisco Bay Area.  In  1988 I began Donna Hunt Design Studios which is now celebrating it’s 31st year in business.  That studio is now located on my property in the mountain town of La Honda surrounded by magnificent Redwoods and the pounding Pacific Ocean only 15 minutes away.  After 40 years of living in California I’ve landed in this small mountain town, whose inhabitants are out spoken individuals, living self sustaining, environmentally positive lives and trying their best at leaving as small a carbon footprint as is possible.  These people gravitated here decades ago and began planting the first seeds towards what is now known as an ever-expanding, organic food eating, self sufficient, socially active movement we see  happening around us today.  La Honda;s version has always had the more modern idea of  "Live and Let Live".  Our choice has always been choosing not to profit but to simply live, letting others live as they see fit.  Generally  speaking it's worked pretty well with a rich history you might be able to hear a little bit about from some of the locals, if your lucky.  Artists, musicians business-people and teachers are a few examples of La Honda’s inhabitants who find themselves living and working together in a renaissance-style existence.  Out spoken individuals living in their quiet mountain home town surrounded by magnificent Redwood trees on this beautiful planet within 15 minutes of the  stunning Pacific Ocean.  What’s important is right under our feet, connecting us all to one another,  and celebrating all that we have!

I have a new roommate, Matt who 's currently helping me on the land with me these days and it could be exactly what I"ve been needing.  It's a spectacular place to live but the mountains have a way of shedding all that they have in them, right through the windows and into your house.   Constant attention to keeping the place tidy is a a serious affair it's sometimes gotten in the way of my art glass business, also located here on the land.  Having someone here helping me out is making all the difference in the world and I can see many  positive changes already.  Matt lives in a small cottage at the back of the property.  He'll soon be set up nicely.  He kieeps to himself but is happy to be available to guests with any questions or assistance  that you might have while staying here with us  His space is a detached building and very private and sports a studio-style bedroom with a small kitchenette .  He uses the big house for meals and the bathroom facilities. He's instrumental in helping me with the upkeep of the 1/2 acre front yard area as well as the wilderness areas behind my home.  I am close to being the last house in the southwest section of the town  of La Honda.  This makes my nearest neighbor s in that direction many miles away with  only woods between us.  When I say woods, I mean numerous varieties of Oak, Douglass Fiir and of course the amazing Redwoods Trees that survive only in this region of the world  It's possible that my nearest neighbor in that direction could all the way to the coastal town of Pescadero some 15 miles away.  Out my back door there's forest for all the eyes can see  before running into the c community of Pescadero.

So come on in, I’ll tell you of the local "sweet spots" including live locaI music venues, Art and Wine Festivals, Mavericks Surf Competitions, or simply the quiet, beautiful hikes you can take right out my back door.  You' ll be glad you did.  I am the primary Inn Keeper but both Matt and I are here on the property and we'll see to it a good time is had by all.  In the words of Tom Bodett of Motel 6 and all the  other comedic formats which paved the road to his fame and fortunes, "We'll leave the light on!"  Finally it's only Thirteen miles, about 25 minutes to the famed birth place of technology, the Silicon Valley.  As close as that seems, it couldn't be further away, in every respect.  Many La Hondan's couldn't be happier about that as we pace ourselves into the later years of our lives.

Cheers from our small family,
Donna Hunt Dusse

The winter snow kept coming and they eventually ran out of medicine and food. Unfortunately, they had to resort to cannibalism to survive, which the majority did.

He made a fortune selling gold mining equipment when the gold rush came in 1848-49 and bought a huge swath of land. After him and his children's passing, the property was sectioned up and divided into what is today, Downtown San Jose.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

host_about:
Eileen was raised in the Midwest in a little farm town called Trenton, IL (population of 2500) since she was 5 years old. Trenton is about an hour from St. Louis, MO.  In August 1993, my two sisters and I quit our jobs in Chicago and decided to travel the world. Our two year travel binge took us to the Caribbean, Europe & Asia.  Finally, in December 1994, we started our trek back home from Asia with one more stop. A 5-day layover in….. SAN FRANCISCO.  Little did we know that the layover would be our destiny.  That’s when we fell in love, not with boys, but with the city.  I knew the next stage of my life would begin here. About the Inner Mission District-
"La Mision" / The MIssion
Centrally located close to downtown, it is the city's Latino district & has been the gateway for most new immigrants, initially Italian, Irish, then predominantly Latino since the 1970's .
It is famous for its historic buildings, Mission burritos (the best in Northern California), grungy artistic scene & it's colorful murals.
Though the Mission still retains it's gritty 'barrio' (hood) flavor the neighborhood has been undergoing a second wave of gentrification, experiencing with an influx of techn money.
The Mission district is large & complex, with varying socioeconomic areas, clusters of mini-communities, and specialty stores found nowhere else. A few years back Utne Reader rated the Inner Mission the 2nd coolest place to live in the US (first was New Orlean's Garden District).
Like in any other cities there are sections of the Mission that can be high crime but don't let that scare you, a
host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.
- See the Zapatista Mural in Jack Kerouc Alley, painted by a dear friend &  behind iconic City Lights Bookstore .  Ask me about the mural story.
-Catch a baseball game at Oracle park !

Huey Lewis & the News 
Carlos Santana  & more !

Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

Welcome to HacknSleep! Hacknsleep provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

neighborhood_overview:
This area belonged to James Reed, who was one of the leaders of the "Donnor Party." They were a group of settlers that came to California from Nevada in the 1800's with wagons and horses. They were making their way through what is today Lake Tahoe, when they got snowed in. With no way to continue forward through the thick snow, they decided to make camp. The winter snow kept coming and they eventually ran out of medicine and food. Unfortunately, they had to resort to cannibalism to survive, which the majority did.
After that terrible tragedy, one of the leaders, James Reed, made his home in what is today, Downtown San Jose. He made a fortune selling gold mining equipment when the gold rush came in 1848-49 and bought a huge swath of land. After him and his children's passing, the property was sectioned up and divided into what is today, Downtown San Jose.

by Anna Medina/ Palo Alto Weekly

Over the years, the Old Palo Alto neighborhood has garnered a reputation for housing some of the wealthiest, most influential residents in town. It's not, for example, uncommon to see tourists stop by the late Steve Jobs' home, and the neighborhood is peppered with ongoing construction sites, where modern mansions are replacing older homes.

The face of Old Palo Alto is rapidly changing, but a stroll through the quiet, tree-lined neighborhood with its shaded sidewalks and fragrant gardens, can offer a glimpse of-- or even a feel for-- Old Palo Alto's past, and an understanding of why it is and has long been such a coveted spot in town.

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry!

Redwoods and the sea in one idyllic setting!

neighborhood_overview:
Music City Hotel is located in the vibrant Polk Gulch/Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

Tourist attractions and neighborhoods
host_about: You will be energized by the past, present and future of music during your stay at Music City Hotel – a tribute to the robust musical history of the Bay Area, and dedicated towards nurturing its present and future. Immerse yourself in our stylishly decorated rooms while staying connected at the crossroads of the city’s present day music scene, along with its storied past.

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

name: Condo in San Francisco · ★5.0 · 3 bedrooms · 3 beds · 2 baths
neighborhood_overview:
Our building is located in the centrally-located NOPA district filled with some of the most beautiful architecture in the City. We're only two blocks from the world famous Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies. A block away is the vibrant Divisadero corridor with its trendy restaurants, BiRite supermarket, a San Francisco institution and numerous coffee shops.

We just minutes walking distance from the best outdoor spaces the City has to offer: Golden Gate Park begins at the Panhandle with its plethora of walking and biking paths, green meadows, groves and fields. The Park continues westward all the way to the Pacific ocean and the Golden Gate Bridge. On the way, you'll see flowers, bodies of water with resident ducks and geese, even a small herd of resident bison. Alamo Square Park is fast becoming the City's premier dog park, popular with picnicers. A little further away is Duboce Triangle Park, surrounded by classic Victorians and famous for its off-lease doggy area.

He is a font of information on all things cool happening in the City, while I am the handyman, geeky technology guy who keeps the house running - its (usually) a perfect match. We've gotten to really explore the City together and there always seems to be a new place to go see. A perfect day for us in the City: Hiking one of the many spectacular hiking and biking trails in the City or Marin Headlands, then a nice dinner at a trendy restaurant (even if its takeout), then a movie at home. Our apartment is kept immaculately clean and functioning, and we want our guests to feel warm and welcome. We enjoy a good relationship with our neighbors, so we're always careful to tell guests to be respectful of them also.

host_about:
Built by the son of a California Gold Rush miner, the historic Marina Motel was built to celebrate the opening of the Golden Gate Bridge in the late 1930's and is still run by the same family. Ideally situated between Fisherman's Wharf and the Golden Gate Bridge in the popular Marina District, the Marina Motel offers a one-of-a-kind, old world experience. The first impression one has upon stepping into the motel's cobblestone courtyard is "Wow! This is like a little oasis back here with birds chirping, flowers EVERYWHERE, cute little garages and rooms decorated to feel like home. I feel like I'm in Europe."

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

host_about:
I have just ventured into Airbnb and aim to make the world more hospitable by opening up a beautiful room in my lovely 1930s house for travelers across the United States and around the World. Within one month I have had the pleasure of hosting over a half dozen guests from New York, Los Angeles, Pennsylvania, China, Japan, Spain.  I enjoy hosting people that are professional, clean, and respectful, and treat my home and room with the same care they would treat their own home.


What is being offered here is a well-furnished room with a queen bed and a bathroom for exclusive use of the guest(s). Thank you for checking out this beautiful home that's close to everything San Jose has to offer. Because the house is close to the San Jose airport, Silicon Valley companies, Levi's and Avaya stadiums, SAP Center, The Convention Center, and downtown San Jose it has become a popular place for guests - business people and tourists alike.

Opening up my home to Airbnb guests is very new to me and I'm still learning from every new guest experience and using that experience to make the next guest's stay more comfortable. Examples include: making a bottle of water available for every guest, filling the biscuit barrel with biscuits or chocolates, adding a lock to the room (there wasn't one previously), buying a hair dryer (being a guy I never thought that that some women would ask for it), providing an iron. However, I have spent more than 1,200 nights at a number of hotel chains - Marriott (my favorite), Starwood, The Ritz Carlton, Four Seasons, and have borrowed these experiences in making guest stays more comfortable. While you will find both lower priced and higher priced rooms in the area I price the room based on certain minimum standards required to maintain the place. As a result, you will find that my prices are not quite as low as some of the motels in the area, but they are nowhere as high as a major hotel. If you like a beautiful, clean room, at a reasonable price you will not be disappointed!

Lastly, I'm a big proponent of the "sharing economy" and believe that we need to put more of our assets to work - that includes our homes, our cars, and our time - to create economic opportunities and uplift for all! As an example, much of the proceeds from Airbnb goes towards paying for the upkeep of the house - the groundsman, pool service, and cleaning staff. More people busy and working means lower taxes, less government, and more citizens taking care of their own needs.

neighborhood_overview:
Cleveland Heights
Oakland’s Cleveland Heights neighborhood occupies the sloping hills in the northwestern corner of the city’s San Antonio district. Encompassing the historic Haddon Hill and Peralta Heights developments, Cleveland Heights offers hilltop views of the lake and Downtown skyline, surrounded by homes and buildings comprising a variety of early-1900s architectural styles.

Cleveland Heights lies just east of Lake Merritt – residents can take the steep, circa-1920s staircase park of Cleveland Cascade down to the 3.4 miles of waterfront paths and green space. Haddon Hill Café is a neighborhood favorite for coffee and pastries, while nearby Champa Garden serves all types of delicious Asian noodles. Quintessential neighborhood dive Baggy’s by the Lake is a time-honored treasure, and the Lakeshore and Grand Lake shopping districts, each full of bars, restaurants, grocery stores, and other amenities – including the weekly Grand Lake Farmer’s Market – are nearby.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

This area belonged to James Reed, who was one of the leaders of the "Donnor Party." They were a group of settlers that came to California from Nevada in the 1800's with wagons and horses. They were making their way through what is today Lake Tahoe, when they got snowed in. With no way to continue forward through the thick snow, they decided to make camp. The winter snow kept coming and they eventually ran out of medicine and food. Unfortunately, they had to resort to cannibalism to survive, which the majority did.
After that terrible tragedy, one of the leaders, James Reed, made his home in what is today, Downtown San Jose. He made a fortune selling gold mining equipment when the gold rush came in 1848-49 and bought a huge swath of land. After him and his children's passing, the property was sectioned up and divided into what is today, Downtown San Jose.

While we accept shorter reservations, we specialize in providing furnished homes for 1-12 months, and have noticed many of our customers are business travelers and travel nurses. As a former employee traveling for work in the finance industry, I realized that staying in hotels for long periods wasn't all it was chalked up to be... and that I could help provide a better experience for other travelers also. 

I've hosted hundreds of guests from around the US and world, and have studios to 2 bedroom apartments around the San Francisco Bay Area and Silicon Valley: 
- Mountain View
- San Jose
- Redwood City
- Oakland (quick commute to San Francisco)
- Richmond

Send me a message and let's see what we can find closest to your work that meets your needs.

I LOVE the San Francisco Bay Area, and I want you to also! I've lived here for over a decade, and there may be no other place in the world that offers the mix of opportunity, great weather, beautiful nature, urban activities, events, concerts, sporting events, and all kinds of great people.

I'll provide you my own local guide of activities, meetups for your personal interests, and do my best to enjoying your time in the Bay, being productive, staying active, and making the most of your time here (or you're welcome to relax.. we're just here when you need us.)

I have personally stayed in over 25 different Airbnb apartments around the US and the world, so I also know a thing or two about what makes a great furnished home and host. And will do my best to provide that to you. 

A little more about me personally: I've lived in California my whole life, and graduated from San Francisco State University, with a major in Economics and minor in Finance. I've lived all over the Bay Area, including most of the homes I host on Airbnb. I used to work for the State of California in bank regulation, before providing furnished homes and great stays to my guests full-time. 

I enjoy learning and sharing with other Airbnb hosts and real estate investors. In my free time, I also enjoy water color painting, karaoke, beaches, traveling, and making people happy :) 

I realize the San Francisco Bay Area gets very busy and can be quite pricey relative to other locations, so please send me a message so I can see what affordable home we can get you, before everything gets booked up. Thank you for your time.

The Old Oakland district was the "original" downtown Oakland during the 1860s after Central Pacific Railroad constructed a terminus on 7th Street. By the 1870s, elegant brick Victorian hotels were being built in the blocks surrounding the railroad station to accommodate travelers. The ground floor of the hotels were designed as series of narrow shops so that pedestrians would pass by many of them just walking down the block. The architectural styles of the time featured tall, cast-iron columns and large plate-glass windows.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

host_about:
Sharing spaces that I have designed is both a business and a passion with this year marking my 20th season in Lake Tahoe.  Over the years many rental clients have become good friends and return each year to the same property.  Being the host to these return guests is the most rewarding part of my vacation and short term rental work. .

After spending my adult years raising my family on a sheep farmlett in Sebastopol California  with summer and weekend visits to  Lake Tahoe, got the travel bug and found an opportunity for change so change happened.

Buenos Aires is where I now spend about half of my time, por razon de tango (because of tango) but also because it is a fun and with the internet my work can happen wherever I am in the world.  Argentina is a  random place where strange things always happen.  I have met wonderful, interesting international people who come annually to Argentina to immerse themselves in the tango culture.  My life here is a combination of a Danielle Steele romance novel and a Woody Allen Movie. Taking notes, there is a book in here somewhere.

I have always loved dancing and for the last 10 years it has been a huge part of my life. Now that my children are super responsible adults, it has been possible to pursue it on a more intense level.  Ever since I went to college in Spain, living in a Spanish speaking country had always been my desire. I was invited to Buenos Aires in January 2009 to help teach Lindy Hop, specifically Balboa, at an International Lindy Hop Festival. Went tango dancing one night to Club Gricel and got completely hooked during one tanda de Calo, a composer of romantic tangos. A tanda is a group of 3-4 songs with some type of commonality that you dance with one partner. Tango either speaks to you or it does not, hard to explain but what the locals dance is not the show tango that people usually think of, it is a more personal and intimate experience. 

It has been exciting and never boring living a gypsy lifestyle, being able to travel to cities with varied dance communities, always running into friends from my dance world, managing the rentals all day and tango dancing all night, literally.   Sleep sometimes suffers a bit.  My favorite places to visit (and dance) so far have been Istanbul, Cosquin in Argentna for the annual Folklore festival, Rome, and Paris.  Culturally Turkey was the most amazing trip.  My motto has always been "Press On" but at this very moment staying home is sounding like a fun thing! 

Asides from dancing (swing, salsa, tango, folklore, pretty much everything) I also love to cook so every kitchen is fully equipped.  Hiking, skiing, decorating, design work and music are also my passions.  Read a lot more before tango but still find some time to read.  Suggestions are welcome!

Just rented my first property on Air bnb and it was a great experience, cute beach apartment in Venice California.  This inspired me to list on this site.

In order to keep things running smoothly and also to enjoy all that Northern California has to offer I come back several times a year.  When in the California I go through each San Francisco flat and Tahoe house make sure that all is in order and in good repair. To to be able to offer to visitors to Lake Tahoe and San Francisco lovely spaces where they can enjoy their valuable vacation or  time away from home for a project is a pleasure.

neighborhood_overview:
Historical Telegraph Hill ( VERY SAFE AREA)
Now: The iconic Coit Tower is the focal point of the area for most visitors, but if you're willing to take your time and wander (and hike a couple of steep stretches of steps) you can catch a lot of extra scenery. Many people take the Greenwich Street steps since they are closest to the tower, and return the same way. The Filbert Street steps, just to the south, lead through much more of the lush landscaping characteristic of Telegraph Hill. Our neighborhood is also known for supporting a flock of feral parrots, primarily red-masked parakeets (Aratinga erythrogenys), descended from escaped or released pets. The flock was popularized by a book and subsequent documentary (2003), both titled The Wild Parrots of Telegraph Hill.

Then: The name Telegraph Hill came from a structure built on the top of the hill in the mid-1800s, which would visually signal the city with regard to the type of vessels passing through the Golden Gate.

Our Farmhouse was built in 1932 during a thriving area for Live Oak as the crown jewel of hens and egg production. The chickens are gone but their history has left us with rich fertile soil where we have taken advantage of this resource to plant a flourishing garden.

Live Oak and Santa Cruz raised the second most number of chickens in the State after Petaluma, in the heyday of egg production in the first half of the 20th century. Chanticleer Ave is named after the Chanticleer Rooster, and Live Oak was the epicenter, being the location of the local Farmer’s Exchange, an enterprise modeled after the mid west member-owned Co-ops. Two trains a day brought ingredients for chicken feed to the Exchange and they were milled and blended into feed for the members.

Live Oak is rich in history and we welcome you to explore our quiet neighborhood and discover all kinds of wonderful hidden gems.

host_about:
I love having guests and I'll do everything I can to make sure you have a wonderful stay in my home.  I'm especially proud of my status as a Superhost and I work hard to maintain that (we're re-evaluated every 3 months). Even after 9 years as a host I feel like every guest is a new friend and look forward to meeting them. 

For those guests new to Airbnb, I want to make sure your first experience is a complete success; and for those who’ve stayed in an Airbnb before, I want to make sure your stay with me is the best you've experienced.

A little about me. I'm sort of retired, after 20+ years as a software engineer, and a couple of other careers as well. 

Things I like to do:  travel, hike, cook, garden, bicycle, train dogs, go to art galleries, of which we have many in the Bay Area, opera, ballet and the theater, and spend time with friends and family.  I especially like DIY projects on my own home. 

I've been interested in California native plants for a while and I'm beginning to add them to my yard. Recently I've become a Master Gardener so these days I spend a lot of time outside, often in Alum Rock Park and on plants and gardening. 

Another of my passions is working with rescued dogs, especially German Shepherd Dogs. I also volunteer with our Wildlife Center of Silicon Valley taking care of injured and orphaned wildlife and releasing them back into the wild.

My experience with Airbnb has been fantastic! Meeting lots of new people from many different cultures, I'm learning about those cultures and countries, and finding out about ethnic restaurants nearby that I've never tried. All my 300+ guests, from 25 countries, have been wonderful.  I've been very lucky and thank Airbnb for their part in making my experience such a good one. 

Several of my guests have found permanent homes here in Silicon Valley and I love to get together with them.

I’m looking forward to meeting you.

I'm a licensed Realtor, original music artist, video producer, and communications specialist who loves to BBQ, entertain, meet new people, and travel. I have two wonderful teens who live with me part time and family is very important to me.

I've loved watching our city grow over the years, locally known as "The Town" for our rich diversity, colorful history, and down to earth people. 

There are dozens of new restaurants, brew pubs, and shops flooding into Oakland as the cost of living and doing business in San Francisco continues to rise. The NBA Championship Golden State Warriors introduced Oakland to the world in a positive light, and the Oakland International Airport is small, super convenient, and minutes away. 

Visit our charming 1922 California Bungalow in the beautiful Maxwell Park neighborhood of Oakland, CA. Take BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) to San Francisco ("The City") to avoid parking hassles while there. I've also put together a list of cool things to do right here in Oakland...on the "Sunny Side of the Bay!"

ABOUT MY TWO LISTINGS:

1) PRIVATE COZY COTTAGE:
We know you'll love our beautiful completely private (detached) carriage house with kitchenette, granite bar, microwave, mini-fridge, coffee maker, hardwood floors, natural light, gas heat, flatscreen TV with Roku, Netflix, and Prime Movies. There's also FREE Wifi, a music dock, open tile shower, and FREE parking in a great neighborhood. The queen sofa bed has a 2 inch memory foam topper so you'll sleep like a dream!

This private spacious bedroom is perfect for a single guest, or two adventurers traveling together in need two full-sized pillow-top bunk beds and locking doors. Our lovely 1922 California Bungalow offers guests a clean, comfortable, stylish place to stay in a centrally located great neighborhood with free parking. I recently added a 32 inch flat screen TV with Netflix, RoKu, and Prime movies. 

Come and go as you please through a lovely private gated backyard with redwood deck, outdoor seating, seasonal fire pit, flowers, and organic gardens. Enjoy your new cozy home away from home!

I look forward to hosting you,

--Colette

neighborhood_overview: Once a shopping district in the early 20th century, Uptown is the hottest neighborhood in Oakland. A new restaurant, indie boutique, or bar seemingly opens every other week, with nearly 125 opened in the past decade. Billed as the arts and entertainment district of Oakland, it fulfills its promise, particularly during the boisterous Art Murmur on First Fridays. But the prettiest art may be the Art Deco buildings themselves, with the crown jewels being the show stopping Fox and the Paramount theaters. The former is mostly a live music venue; the latter channels its inner flapper often (classic movies with a live organ player). Art galleries, run by the artists or by volunteers, are opening in brick warehouses. Down side streets are scenes of the start-up, DIY revolution with co-ops, an urban winery, entrepreneur hubs, and creative centers.

"La Mision"

Though the Mission still retains it's gritty 'barrio' (hood) flavor the neighborhood has been undergoing a second wave of gentrification lately and has been experiencing with an influx of technology money.
The Mission district is large & complex, with varying socioeconomic areas, clusters of mini-communities, and specialty stores found nowhere else. A few years back Utne Reader rated the Inner Mission the 2nd coolest place to live in the US (first was New Orlean's Garden District).
